findings.title: The nested-vector panic is turned into an error that says the element type has no Go…
findings.claim: The nested-vector panic is turned into an error that says the element type has no Go type, even though one exists. The real cause is left in place: the inner vector's custom name is cut down to the bare "...VectorType" prefix.

findings.title: The VectorType branch of getCassandraLongType still falls back to a nameless custom type…
findings.claim: The VectorType branch of getCassandraLongType still falls back to a nameless custom type when parsing the dimension fails. The PR's new behaviour of keeping the unrecognised name was applied only to the basic-type branch.

findings.title: The function-level comment says "every path below turns it into an allocation (make,…
findings.claim: The function-level comment says "every path below turns it into an allocation (make, reflect.MakeSlice)". That is not true for the array destination, or for vectorSliceReuse when the destination already has enough capacity. The PR's own test comment contradicts it.

findings.title: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating asserts on process-wide runtime
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating asserts on process-wide runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc. Being non-parallel only keeps other top-level tests paused. Background goroutines left by earlier unit tests, and the -race runtime used by make test-unit, also count toward TotalAlloc.

findings.title: The test for a decodable element type pins Zero()'s []*float32 result
findings.claim: The test for a decodable element type pins Zero()'s []*float32 result. That pointer-element slice disagrees with goType, which strips the pointer and gives []float32.

findings.title: The new makeVectorType copies the bodies of the existing makeDoubleVectorType and…
findings.claim: The new makeVectorType copies the bodies of the existing makeDoubleVectorType and makeFloat32VectorType (and vector_bench_test.go's makeFloatVectorType) instead of having them delegate to it.

findings.title: The commit messages do not follow CONTRIBUTING
findings.claim: The commit messages do not follow CONTRIBUTING.md's required format. They use a lowercase conventional 'fix(marshal):' prefix rather than a short description starting with a capital letter, and neither has the 'Patch by <authors>; reviewed by <Reviewers> for #####' line. Recent repository history uses the same conventional style, so the rule may be stale.

findings.title: These are notable behaviour changes (new Scan errors instead of panics, and new error…
findings.claim: These are notable behaviour changes (new Scan errors instead of panics, and new error text for unknown custom types), but nothing in the change documents them in a changelog or godoc. The checklist requires that.

findings.title: The TestVectorElemMinSize comment says a zero-dimension vector cannot describe an…
findings.claim: The TestVectorElemMinSize comment says a zero-dimension vector cannot describe an element in zero bytes. A fixed-element vector<float,0> encodes in exactly zero bytes, so the floor of 1 is an over-approximation, not a fact.

findings.title: The TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads doc says the bound is non-narrowing and…
findings.claim: The TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads doc says the bound is non-narrowing and that 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes'. That is false for vector<vector<float,0>,N>, whose valid encoding is 0 bytes, and the bound rejects it.

findings.title: The new bound and the existing fast path sit next to each other, and each is guarded by…
findings.claim: The new bound and the existing fast path sit next to each other, and each is guarded by its own copy of `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil`. The fast path's safety depends on running after the bound, because the bound is what keeps `Dimensions*8` from wrapping.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize saturates at math
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize saturates at math.MaxInt32, an unexplained limit. The function returns `int` and does its arithmetic in int64, and the only stated reason is 'saturate rather than wrap'.

findings.title: The new nil-Type guard builds its own error after VectorType
findings.claim: The new nil-Type guard builds its own error after VectorType.Zero() has already discarded the more specific error from goType/NewWithError ("cannot create Go type for unknown CQL type %s"). unmarshalList takes the other route and propagates goType's error. Two classifiers now answer "what Go type does this element have" for an *any destination.

findings.title: The getCassandraLongType change is not limited to vector errors
findings.claim: The getCassandraLongType change is not limited to vector errors. Every unknown long type name parsed through it (vector subtypes, collections and tuples nested in them, asVectorType/goType) now carries a non-empty custom field. That changes NativeType equality, Custom() and String(), and the text of goType's "cannot create Go type for unknown CQL type %s" for those types.

findings.title: The new makeVectorType test helper takes a Type enum and a separate Java class-name…
findings.claim: The new makeVectorType test helper takes a Type enum and a separate Java class-name string that must agree. Nothing ties them together, so it is a data clump.

findings.title: unmarshalVector recomputes vectorElemMinSize (recursively) on every call
findings.claim: unmarshalVector recomputes vectorElemMinSize (recursively) on every call. For nested vectors the inner unmarshalVector runs once per outer element, so the same inner minimum is computed N times.

findings.title: The new bound comment says 'unmarshalList does the same', but unmarshalList uses a fixed…
findings.claim: The new bound comment says 'unmarshalList does the same', but unmarshalList uses a fixed 4-byte divisor and only applies it to slices, not arrays. The bound here is per-type and covers arrays too.

findings.title: The new test comment says the overflow cases "use the word size so the wrap lands on a…
findings.claim: The new test comment says the overflow cases "use the word size so the wrap lands on a 32-bit target too", but the unit-tagged test package for `gocql` does not compile for a 32-bit `int`, so that target is never exercised.

findings.title: The PR body says 'Every new test fails against pristine marshal
findings.claim: The PR body says 'Every new test fails against pristine marshal.go/helpers.go'. Several added tests cannot fail on pristine code. TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads, TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType, and the 'still decodes' subtests pin existing behaviour. TestVectorElemMinSize would fail to compile, which is not a test failure.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 for a fixed-element inner vector with 0 dimensions, but such…
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 for a fixed-element inner vector with 0 dimensions, but such an element really takes 0 bytes on the wire. A vector<vector<float,0>,N> with an empty non-NULL payload used to decode and is now rejected. The test comment "Neither can describe an element in zero bytes" is wrong for the 0-dimension case.

findings.title: For the nested-vector case the new error cannot say which type the server sent
findings.claim: For the nested-vector case the new error cannot say which type the server sent. VectorType has no String method, so %v of the inner VectorType uses NativeType.String and renders "custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)", with no element type or dimension.

findings.title: A NULL value for a vector column with negative metadata dimensions now errors for a…
findings.claim: A NULL value for a vector column with negative metadata dimensions now errors for a `*[]T` destination but still succeeds for a `**[]T` destination. The PR's behaviour-change section does not mention this.

findings.title: Both commits end with a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' trailer, and the PR body ends…
findings.claim: Both commits end with a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' trailer, and the PR body ends with 'Generated with Claude Code'. The user's standing instructions forbid this attribution in commits and PR descriptions.

findings.title: The getCassandraLongType change applies to every unrecognised type name in all metadata…
findings.claim: The getCassandraLongType change applies to every unrecognised type name in all metadata parsing, not only to vector elements. The PR's 'Behaviour change' section does not mention it.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recurses into a nested VectorType's SubType without a nil check
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize recurses into a nested VectorType's SubType without a nil check. The new comment states that callers of Unmarshal may leave SubType nil.

findings.title: The old fast-path comment says "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path"
findings.claim: The old fast-path comment says "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path". It now sits under the new bound, which rejects an empty non-nil payload whenever Dimensions > 0 before it can reach either path.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize clamps a zero-dimension inner vector to a 1-byte minimum
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize clamps a zero-dimension inner vector to a 1-byte minimum. A test comment then says "Neither can describe an element in zero bytes", but a fixed-type vector<float,0> encodes in exactly 0 bytes. The bound is therefore not "non-narrowing" as TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads claims.

findings.title: The new makeVectorType helper copies the bodies of the existing makeDoubleVectorType and…
findings.claim: The new makeVectorType helper copies the bodies of the existing makeDoubleVectorType and makeFloat32VectorType, and vector_bench_test.go's makeFloatVectorType, instead of having those call it. It also takes the CQL Type and the Java class name as two separate parameters that nothing checks against each other.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType now keeps the server's class name only on the unknown-basic-type…
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType now keeps the server's class name only on the unknown-basic-type fallback. Its other degrade-to-custom sites still return a nameless NewNativeType(protoVer, TypeCustom): the map arity error at :222 and the vector dimension parse error at :267. The same function now has inconsistent fallback types.

findings.title: The new count bound reports a short payload as "unmarshal vector: N dimensions do not…
findings.claim: The new count bound reports a short payload as "unmarshal vector: N dimensions do not fit in M bytes", while the float fast paths a few lines below still report a wrong-sized payload as "unmarshal vector<double|float>: expected X bytes, got Y". After this change, which message a user gets for a mis-sized payload depends on whether it is short or long.

findings.title: The new nil-Type guard writes its own message, "unmarshal vector: no Go type for element…
findings.claim: The new nil-Type guard writes its own message, "unmarshal vector: no Go type for element type %v", for the same condition that goType already reports as "cannot create Go type for unknown CQL type %s". VectorType.Zero() swallows that goType error, and the guard does not carry it as the cause.

findings.title: The negative-dimension check runs before the NULL check, so a NULL value for a…
findings.claim: The negative-dimension check runs before the NULL check, so a NULL value for a VectorType with negative Dimensions now returns an error where it used to return nil. The PR's 'Behaviour change' section lists only short and zero-length non-NULL payloads.

findings.title: The bound now runs before destination validation: the non-pointer check, the…
findings.claim: The bound now runs before destination validation: the non-pointer check, the non-empty-interface check, the unsupported-destination fallback, and the array-length mismatch. A short payload combined with a wrong destination now reports the payload size instead of the programming error.

findings.title: A zero-dimensional VectorType with a nil SubType still panics when a non-NULL empty…
findings.claim: A zero-dimensional VectorType with a nil SubType still panics when a non-NULL empty payload is unmarshaled into *any. The new zero-dimension test covers only a concrete slice destination, while the interface path calls info.Zero() before the new nil-Type guard can run.

findings.title: The tests do not exercise the Scan, MapScan, or SliceMap entry points named in the PR's…
findings.claim: The tests do not exercise the Scan, MapScan, or SliceMap entry points named in the PR's crash and diagnostic claims; they invoke unmarshalVector or Unmarshal directly.
